[1.0] By way of present First Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the appellant - insurance company has assailed the impugned judgment and award dated 08.06.2022 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.), Anand (for short "learned Tribunal") in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.172/2016, whereby the learned Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition in favor of the original claimant and awarded Rs.16,78,272/- with interest at the rate of 9%
per annum from the date of claim petition.
[2.0] The brief facts leading to filing of present appeal are as follows:
[2.1] On 04.01.2016, the claimant was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ-23-DA-7152 with moderate speed and on correct side of the road and when he National Insurance Company Ltd vs Ilmuddin Rasulbhai Khokhar on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181294142/
1 reached at the place of accident, driver NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4881/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined of Truck bearing registration No.PB-10-FF-7191 came driving his truck with full speed and while taking turn in excessive speed, dashed the truck with the motorcycle of the original claimant due to which the accident occurred and original claimant sustained serious injuries on his left hand, left shoulder and left side ribs, left leg and also on other parts of his body.
Therefore, the original claimant filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.15 lakh.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
[2.2] After considering the evidence produced on record by the respective parties,
learned Tribunal has been pleased to hold the original opponent No.1 - driver of offending Truck to be solely negligent for the accident.

Hence, present First Appeal is filed by the appellant - insurance company on the ground that the learned Tribunal failed to consider contributory negligence of the claimant as well as on the ground of exorbitant compensation.

[3.0] Learned advocate Mr. Yogi Gadhia appearing for the appellant has submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed an error in not appreciating the fact that even after sustained accidental injuries and disability, there was no loss of pay or retirement benefits to the claimant and relying on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajkumar vs. Ajaykumar & Ors. reported in (2011)1 SCC 343, he has submitted that no compensation ought to have been granted under the head of future loss of income and therefore, learned Tribunal has erred in awarding the compensation to the claimant.

entities.text: Rajkumar vs. Ajaykumar & Ors. reported in (2011)1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, he has requested to allow the appeal.

[4.0] Learned advocate Mr. Nishit Bhalodi appearing for the respondent No.2 - original claimant has opposed the First Appeal on the ground that there is no error committed by the learned Tribunal and just and proper compensation has been awarded by the learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4881/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Tribunal.
Hence, he has requested to dismiss the present appeal.

[5.0] Since the only issue raised in the present appeal is of quantum of compensation and involvement, liability of insurance company and factum of accident is not challenged, present appeal is considered in narrow compass.

[6.0] Having heard learned advocate for the appellant - insurance company and learned advocate for the original claimant and perusing the record, it appears that the learned Tribunal has considered the evidence produced and adduced by both the parties including the affiadvit of the claimant (Exh.25), complaint (Exh.45),
panchnama of scene of accident (Exh.46) as well as the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi vs. H.R.S.T.C. reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 and Parmeshwari Devi vs. Amir Chand reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, wherein it is held that it is settled law that negligence is required to be proved in claim National Insurance Company Ltd vs Ilmuddin Rasulbhai Khokhar on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181294142/
2 petition under section 166 of the MV Act only on the touchstone of the preponderance of probability and not beyond doubt and even considering the fact that the driver of offending Truck has not stepped into the witness box, learned Tribunal has held the driver of offending Truck to be solely negligent for the accident.
Even otherwise, negligence and liability is not seriously challenged by the learned advocate for the insurance company.
[7.0] Perusing the record & proceedings, it appears that the original claimant filed his affidavit at Exh.25, wherein he has stated that at the time of accident, he was getting income of Rs.26,000/-
p.m. by serving as Dye Maker in Elecon Engineering Company Ltd., at Vallabh Vidhyanagar

sentences.text: and in support of his say, the claimant has examined authorised person Mr. Alpesh Mukundprasad Thakar at Exh.39, who NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4881/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined has stated on oath that, at the time of accident claimant was serving as a Technician in Elecon Engineering Company and produced his salary slips at Exhs.40 and 42, which reveal that, at the time of accident, the claimant was paid monthly salary of Rs. 26,000/- by the company.
However, he has admitted that from his salary, deduction towards professional Tax and Income tax was made.

So, considering evidence of said witness and last salary slip produced at Exh. 40,
deduction of Rs. 200/- and 2000/- (lump sum) towards professional Tax and Income Tax were made and hence, after having this deduction, his net monthly income comes to Rs.23,800/- and therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly considered the monthly income of claimant at Rs.23,800/- which does not call for any interference.

[7.1] The sole contention of the learned advocate appearing for the appellant - insurance company is that since the original claimant was in permanent job and his income has increased day by day even after sustaining the disablement and therefore, learned Tribunal ought not to have awarded future loss of income.
It is needless to say that there is no rule or law that after the accident merely because income has increased, compensation is required to be refused towards future loss of income.

In this regard, reference is required to be made to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain vs. Regional Manager, U.P.
State Road Transport Corporation reported in 2022(0) AIJEL-SC 70212.

sentences.text:
Hence, considering monthly income of the claimant at Rs.23,800/- and as the claimant was aged 58 years of age at the time of accident, in view of decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt)
& Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. [2009 (6) SCC 121], applying multiplier of 9, the learned Tribunal considering 43% of disability body as a whole has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4881/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined awarded Rs.11,05,272/- [Rs.23,800 x 43% (disability) 12 x 9] towards future loss of income, which does not call for any interference.
[7.2] So far as compensation awarded under other heads is concerned, the learned Tribunal has appropriately awarded compensation under the heads of medical expenses, pain, shock and suffering, special diet, attendant & transportation, loss of amenities and artificial leg and future medical expenses and to that extent, no interference is called for at the hands of this Court as even otherwise, the appellant - insurance company has not challenged the same.

sentences.text: Another argument of the learned advocate for the appellant - insurance company is that the original claimant is not entitled to claim interest on the amount of future loss of income.

Herein, the claim petition was filed in the year 2016 however, the impugned judgment and award is passed in the year 2022 and the said delay cannot be attributed to the original claimant as laws' delay cannot,
without proper substantiation, be cast upon the shoulders of one or other party to the lis and in that circumstance necessarily interest must run from the date of filing of the claim petition, to the date of payment for which precedents are legion.

Learned advocate for the insurance company has opposed the claim of the original claimant to award interest on the amount awarded under the head of future loss of income by submitting that compensation under the said head in any event is an amount received in advance, normally inuring to the benefit of the claimants only in future.

However, there was nothing stopping the Insurance Company from settling the claim on a computation, on receipt of intimation of the accident, especially since the determination of compensation for loss of dependency, on death being occasioned in a motor vehicle accident, can be determined as NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4881/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined evident from the judicial precedents; at least provisionally.

In this regard, reference is required to be made to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Niru @
Niharika & Ors. reported in 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 693.

sentences.text: Hence, the argument canvassed by the learned advocate for the appellant - insurance company that the original claimant is not entitled to claim interest on the amount of future loss of income is not accepted.
[9.0] Hence, the compensation as detailed hereinbelow, as awarded by the learned Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for any interference.

Future loss of income Rs.
 Medical Expenses Rs.
 Pain, shock and suffering Rs  Spl.

Diet, attendant and transportation Rs  Loss of amenities Rs  Artificial leg and future medical Rs.
 expenses
Total...
16  [10.0] In wake of aforesaid conspectus, First Appeal is  dismissed.

[10.1] The learned Tribunal is directed to disburse the amount of compensation as deposited by the appellant - insurance company with the learned Tribunal, alongwith accrued interest thereon, if any, to the original claimant, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure and strictly in accordance with the apportionment made by the learned Tribunal.
